title: IFX I2-B: CI evidence design and successor bundle (IFX-V4-006 first)
goal: Fix the slow C6c Linux copy-back (IFX-V4-006), study how the seven evidence producers can run in CI without pinned local locks and without circular V3 ownership, and bring a recommended option to an operator decision before any bundle change.
acceptanceCriteria: The archive copy-back is byte-faithful and faster, with passing harness controls.
The design note covers all seven producers and all 13 context-ownership rows and recommends one option.
No bundle, Profile, module, remote, workflow or ruleset change before the B3 decision.
risks: Re-attesting V3-produced evidence could be mistaken for V4 ownership.
Dropping a live pin could remove a check that depended only on the hash; the A1-2 change specification lists and rewrites such checks.
decisions: IFX-V4-006 is fixed before any new C6c run.
Options D-A, D-B and D-C are compared before choosing.
B3: pin split accepted; D-B in two steps (0.5.0-a PR-gate rework, 0.5.0-b producer relocation).
A1: 0.5.0 lock consumers read locks from EvidenceRoot and verify the producer contract; live pins are dropped, governance pins kept.
